issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect a measurement function named 'dd_measure_all', but the template defines it as 'measure_all_dd'. This name mismatch between template and solution/problem will confuse students (they will implement or be guided by the problem to implement 'dd_measure_all' while the template's provided stub has a different name), and may cause automated tests or student code to fail to find the expected function.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function 'measure_all_dd' to 'dd_measure_all' to match the names used in the problem statement and solution (or update the problem statement and solution to use 'measure_all_dd'). Ensure all references/comments and tests consistently use the same function name.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to the measurement helper as 'dd_measure_all', but the template defines the function as 'measure_all_dd'. This inconsistent identifier ordering for the same conceptual operation (measuring all qubits and returning counts) can confuse students implementing or calling the function because the name differs between the starter code and the expected API in the task description and reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function measure_all_dd to dd_measure_all (and update any local references) so its name matches the problem statement and solution. Alternatively, update the problem statement and solution to use measure_all_dd consistently; prefer aligning the template to the documented API (dd_measure_all) to avoid student confusion.
